hypothesis: The Bluetooth application, USB path and startup deadlines hold under modeled module, scheduler and USB effects.
conclusion: Software evidence only; physical startup time, headset operation and wideband mSBC are unqualified.
narrative: Host-only results from checks that have since been removed (bluetooth-startup-deadline, bluetooth-usb-native shared emulator, bluetooth-repeated-usb). The startup-deadline check executed the application with modeled module readiness and real UART/H4/HCI code in 17 startup cases (first-readiness boundary, a query crossing the boundary, clock and generation refusal, UART/wake/module waits through HCI expiry, the resident anchor, pending firmware beyond the provisional HCI offset) plus one case for the resident headset stage arithmetic, lifetime cap and unchanged supervised offsets. The shared USB emulator supplied task, endpoint and architectural counter models for playback, repeated capture and mSBC checks; the application check imported it and added recognition-specific fixtures and clock hooks. The repeated-capture USB check ran the actual native USB task, serializer, result APIs and TinyUSB for delivery, early and stale acknowledgment, revocation and publication order; the host used their frames to check two-result collection, backlog, durable-store failure, wrong identity, sample gaps, missing disconnect and a 512-byte first USB packet, with scheduler progress, device registers, radio/controller events and USB device effects modeled. No hardware transaction was performed.
